## Refusal census (J264, N-58), re-measured

* **Method.** The script was the checker's own: `census.mts`, run through tsx in the mirror. It took every B-FUZZ unit
  argv of the real manifests and passed it through fuzz-bar's own `run()`. A sentinel `runFuzz` stopped each run right
  after the argument rule. "Before" means each argv with the two Q94 flags removed, which equals the before-image's
  argv.
* **Results.** Each tier has 25 units:

  | tier | refused before | refused after | partition units without the flags (after) |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | PR | 0 | 0 | 0 |
  | PR (fallback) | 0 | 0 | 0 |
  | nightly | 0 | 0 | 0 |
  | milestone | 0 | 0 | 0 |

* **Sanity check.** K4 (both flags put on the whole-set unit) is the shape fuzz-bar refuses with exit 64, and the pins
  kill it.
* **The replay family.** It registers no refusal. A seed that throws counts as a crash, never a refusal, and the
  planted-hang and real-replay probes met none.
* **Outcome.** Lawful-input refusals were 0 before and 0 after, so the count did not rise. No refusal class was met
  that needs a verdict. The kernel refusals that fuzz-bar's insertChain run prints are random-input refusals of
  M0-k-04's family, not this item's.
